title: Kernels of module objects are computed in $\mathcal C$
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a preadditive monoidal category whose tensor product is additive in
each variable, and let $\mathcal R$ be a monoid object of $\mathcal C$. Let
$f\colon M\to N$ be a morphism of $\mathcal R$-module objects ([sk-def-sfb-module-objects])
whose underlying morphism has a kernel $\iota\colon K\to M$ in $\mathcal C$. Then there is
a unique morphism $\gamma_K\colon\mathcal R\otimes K\to K$ with
$\iota\circ\gamma_K=\gamma_M\circ(\mathcal R\otimes\iota)$. It is an action of
$\mathcal R$ on $K$, and $\iota\colon(K,\gamma_K)\to M$ is a kernel of $f$ in
$\Mod_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal C)$.

proof.text: Write $\mu:\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal R\to\mathcal R$ and $\eta:\mathbf1\to\mathcal R$ for multiplication and unit, and compose from right to left. The assumed kernel property means $f\iota=0$ and, for each $a:T\to M$ with $fa=0$, there is a unique $b:T\to K$ with $\iota b=a$. In particular $\iota$ is monic: if $\iota b=\iota c=a$, then $fa=f\iota b=0$, so both $b,c$ are the unique lift of $a$. This cancellation requires no kernel of any other morphism.

source.place: Paragraph 1, the assumed kernel and the cancellations by its inclusion

proof.text:
By [def-weil-preadditive-category], composition with a zero morphism is zero (bilinearity gives $u0=u0+u0$, and cancellation gives $u0=0$, similarly on the other side). By [def-weil-pbc-additive-functor], $\mathcal R\otimes-$ sends the zero morphism to zero: its map on each Hom group is a homomorphism. Thus the underlying zero morphism between any two module objects is a module morphism, since both sides of its linearity equation in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] are zero. Using the same defining linearity equation for $f$ and the kernel equation, put $a=\gamma_M(\mathcal R\otimes\iota)$ and compute
$$fa=f\gamma_M(\mathcal R\otimes\iota)=\gamma_N(\mathcal R\otimes(f\iota))=\gamma_N(\mathcal R\otimes0)=0.$$
The assumed kernel property, applied with $T=\mathcal R\otimes K$, therefore gives a unique $\gamma_K:\mathcal R\otimes K\to K$ with $\iota\gamma_K=\gamma_M(\mathcal R\otimes\iota)$.

source.place: Paragraph 1, first displayed equation and unique factorization

proof.text:
For the unit law of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], naturality of tensoring with $\eta$ and of the left unitor gives
$$\iota\gamma_K(\eta\otimes K)=\gamma_M(\mathcal R\otimes\iota)(\eta\otimes K)=\gamma_M(\eta\otimes M)(\mathbf1\otimes\iota)=\lambda_M(\mathbf1\otimes\iota)=\iota\lambda_K.$$
Cancel the monomorphism $\iota$ by step 1 to obtain $\gamma_K(\eta\otimes K)=\lambda_K$.

source.place: Paragraph 1, the unit axiom after composition with the inclusion

proof.text:
For associativity, write $\alpha_K=\alpha_{\mathcal R,\mathcal R,K}$ and $\alpha_M=\alpha_{\mathcal R,\mathcal R,M}$. Naturality of tensoring with $\mu$, the associativity axiom for $M$ in [sk-def-sfb-module-objects], and naturality of $\alpha$ give
$$\begin{aligned}
\iota\gamma_K(\mu\otimes K)
&=\gamma_M(\mu\otimes M)((\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal R)\otimes\iota)\\
&=\gamma_M(\mathcal R\otimes\gamma_M)\alpha_M((\mathcal R\otimes\mathcal R)\otimes\iota)\\
&=\gamma_M(\mathcal R\otimes\gamma_M)(\mathcal R\otimes(\mathcal R\otimes\iota))\alpha_K\\
&=\gamma_M(\mathcal R\otimes(\iota\gamma_K))\alpha_K
=\iota\gamma_K(\mathcal R\otimes\gamma_K)\alpha_K.
\end{aligned}$$
The penultimate equality is step 2 and functoriality of $\mathcal R\otimes-$. Cancellation by $\iota$ gives precisely the associativity axiom. With step 3 this makes $K$ a module object, and the equation defining $\gamma_K$ is exactly the condition that $\iota$ be a module morphism.

source.place: Paragraph 1, the associativity axiom after composition with the inclusion

proof.text:
Let $L$ be any $\mathcal R$-module object and $g:L\to M$ a module morphism with $fg=0$. The assumed underlying kernel gives a unique $h:L\to K$ with $\iota h=g$. The defining module-map equations of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] yield
$$\iota h\gamma_L=g\gamma_L=\gamma_M(\mathcal R\otimes g)=\gamma_M(\mathcal R\otimes\iota)(\mathcal R\otimes h)=\iota\gamma_K(\mathcal R\otimes h).$$
Cancel $\iota$ to see that $h$ is a module morphism. Equality and composition of module maps are those of their underlying maps, so $\iota h=g$ holds in the module category; any competing module lift has the same underlying lift and hence equals $h$. Also $f\iota=0$ holds in that category by step 2. These are exactly the kernel universal property there. The uniqueness of the action itself was already obtained in step 2.

source.place: Paragraph 2, linearity and uniqueness of the universal lift

proof_origin.place: Paragraphs 1–2, expanded calculations for unit, associativity, zero morphisms and cancellation
